packs.title: Digital Citizenship & Online Safety
packs.subject: Internet Safety
packs.description: 20 scenario-based questions on privacy, passwords, scams and responsible technology use.

questions.question: A classmate sends a suspicious shortened link. What should you do first?
questions.explanation: Links from unknown sources should be verified before opening.

questions.question: Which password is hardest to guess?
questions.explanation: Long, unique passphrases resist common guessing attacks.

questions.question: A website asks for your one-time login code. What is safest?
options: Do not share the code with anyone
Post it on a group chat
questions.explanation: One-time codes are security credentials meant for your own login.

questions.question: What does multi-factor authentication add?
questions.explanation: MFA requires more than one proof of identity.

questions.question: A game account offers free prizes for your password. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Legitimate prize offers do not require revealing your password.

questions.question: Which personal detail should not be posted publicly?
questions.explanation: A home address can expose your physical location.

questions.question: What is phishing?
options: A trick to steal information using fake messages
questions.explanation: Phishing messages impersonate trusted sources to obtain secrets.

questions.question: A message claims “Act in two minutes or lose your account.” What is a warning sign?
questions.explanation: Scammers often manufacture urgency to reduce careful checking.

questions.question: Which action protects a shared classroom tablet?
options: Sign out after using your account
questions.explanation: Signing out limits later access to your account.

questions.question: What is the safest response to online bullying?
options: Save evidence and tell a trusted adult
questions.explanation: Reporting and seeking help is safer than escalation or retaliation.

questions.question: Which data practice is safest for a student quiz?
options: Collect only information needed for participation
questions.explanation: Data minimization reduces privacy risk.

questions.question: Why should a school app use HTTPS?
options: It encrypts data while travelling over the network
questions.explanation: HTTPS protects data in transit, but does not fix every security issue.

questions.question: A browser warns that a certificate is invalid. What should you do?
questions.explanation: An invalid certificate can indicate an unsafe connection.

questions.question: Why is updating software important?
questions.explanation: Security patches can close known vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Which permission is unnecessary for a basic maths quiz?
questions.explanation: A basic quiz usually does not need access to your contacts.

questions.question: A stranger online asks where you are studying today. What is safest?
options: Share a classroom photo with location
Do not reveal your live location
questions.explanation: Live location information can put privacy and safety at risk.

questions.question: What does a privacy setting control?
options: Who can access certain account information
The length of a school holiday
questions.explanation: Privacy settings manage visibility and data sharing.

questions.question: A friend has shared a password with you. What is appropriate?
options: Encourage them to change it and keep it private
questions.explanation: Credentials should not be reused or distributed.

questions.question: Why should files be backed up?
options: To recover important work after loss or damage
questions.explanation: Backups support recovery when files are lost or damaged.

questions.question: Which rule helps identify an AI-generated claim?
options: Check reliable sources before believing it
Accept it because it sounds confident
questions.explanation: AI can make mistakes, so important claims need independent verification.

packs.title: Science: Plants, Energy & Ecosystems
packs.subject: Science
packs.description: 20 science questions about living systems, food webs, materials and everyday energy.

questions.question: Which part of a plant absorbs most water from soil?
questions.explanation: Roots take up water and dissolved minerals.

questions.question: What gas do plants mainly take in during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water to make sugars.

questions.question: What do we call an animal that eats only plants?
questions.explanation: Herbivores feed on plants.

questions.question: Which organism is a producer in a food chain?
questions.explanation: Grass makes its own food using sunlight.

questions.question: What is evaporation?
options: Liquid water changing into water vapour
questions.explanation: During evaporation liquid particles escape into the gas phase.

questions.question: Which process forms water droplets on a cold glass?
questions.explanation: Water vapour cools and condenses into droplets.

questions.question: Which energy source is renewable?
questions.explanation: Sunlight is replenished naturally and is renewable.

questions.question: What happens when a torch battery runs out of usable energy?
questions.explanation: A torch needs an energy source to keep producing light.

questions.question: Which material usually conducts electricity well?
questions.explanation: Copper has mobile electrons that support electrical conduction.

questions.question: Why does a metal spoon feel cooler than a wooden spoon in the same room?
options: Wood is always hotter than air
Metal conducts heat away from the hand faster
questions.explanation: The difference is mainly heat transfer, not necessarily temperature.

questions.question: What is a food web?
options: A network of connected food chains
questions.explanation: Food webs represent multiple feeding relationships.

questions.question: Why are decomposers important?
options: They recycle nutrients from dead material
questions.explanation: Decomposers break down remains and return nutrients to ecosystems.

questions.question: Which organ helps humans exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide?
questions.explanation: Gas exchange occurs in the lungs.

questions.question: What is a simple example of a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Rusting forms new substances.

questions.question: Which force pulls a dropped ball toward Earth?
questions.explanation: Earth's gravity attracts masses toward its centre.

questions.question: When a shadow becomes shorter at midday, what mainly changed?
options: The Sun's apparent position in the sky
questions.explanation: The sunlight angle changes the length of a shadow.

questions.question: Which change could harm a pond ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Waste pollution can damage organisms and water quality.

questions.question: Which structure protects a plant cell and helps it keep shape?
questions.explanation: Plant cell walls provide support outside the cell membrane.

questions.question: Which tool measures air temperature?
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature.

questions.question: Why do scientists repeat experiments?
options: To check whether results are reliable
questions.explanation: Repeating trials helps identify variability and reliability.

packs.title: English: Grammar in Real Life
packs.subject: English
packs.description: 20 practical English punctuation, vocabulary, sentence and comprehension questions.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She gone to school every day.
She goes to school every day.
She go to school every day.
questions.explanation: The third-person singular present tense uses goes.

questions.question: Choose the correct past-tense sentence.
questions.explanation: Visited is the regular past tense of visit.

questions.question: Which word is an adverb in “He spoke quietly”?
questions.explanation: Quietly describes how he spoke.

questions.question: Choose the correct article: “I saw ___ elephant.”
questions.explanation: Elephant begins with a vowel sound, so an is appropriate.

questions.question: Choose the correct plural of “child.”
questions.explanation: Children is an irregular plural.

questions.question: Choose the correct possessive form meaning the bag belongs to one girl.
questions.explanation: The apostrophe before s marks one girl's possession.

questions.question: Which sentence is a question?
options: Where did you put the keys?
questions.explanation: It directly asks for information.

questions.question: Choose the correct conjunction: “I stayed home ___ it was raining.”
questions.explanation: Because explains the reason for staying home.

questions.question: What is an antonym of “generous”?
questions.explanation: Selfish contrasts with being willing to give.

questions.question: What is a synonym of “enormous”?
questions.explanation: Enormous and huge both mean very large.

questions.question: Choose the correct contraction for “do not.”
questions.explanation: Don't is the contraction of do not.

questions.question: Which word is an adjective in “The bright moon shone”?
questions.explanation: Bright describes the moon.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: “The book is ___ the table.”
questions.explanation: On describes the book's position on the table.

questions.question: Which punctuation ends an exclamation?
questions.explanation: An exclamation mark expresses strong feeling or surprise.

questions.question: Choose the correct conditional: “If it rains, we ___ indoors.”
questions.explanation: Will stay describes a possible future result.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a topic sentence?
options: To introduce the paragraph's main idea
questions.explanation: A topic sentence helps readers understand a paragraph's focus.

questions.question: Which sentence uses quotation marks correctly?
questions.explanation: Quotation marks enclose the exact words spoken.

questions.question: Choose the correct comparative form of “good.”
questions.explanation: Better is the irregular comparative form of good.

questions.question: What is a reliable way to support a factual claim in a report?
questions.explanation: Evidence from trustworthy sources supports factual writing.

questions.question: What is the difference between a fact and an opinion?
options: A fact can be checked against evidence
questions.explanation: A factual statement is testable; an opinion expresses a judgement or preference.

packs.title: Malaysia & World Geography Explorer
packs.subject: Geography
packs.description: 20 geography questions focused on Malaysia, maps, weather and world regions.

questions.question: What is the capital city of Malaysia?
questions.explanation: Kuala Lumpur is Malaysia's national capital; Putrajaya is the federal administrative centre.

questions.question: Which island is Penang Island connected to by the Penang Bridge?
questions.explanation: The bridge connects Penang Island to the mainland of Peninsular Malaysia.

questions.question: What is the state capital of Penang?
questions.explanation: George Town is the capital of the state of Penang.

questions.question: Which Malaysian state is located on the island of Borneo?
questions.explanation: Sabah and Sarawak are Malaysian states on Borneo.

questions.question: Which strait lies between Peninsular Malaysia and Sumatra?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Malacca lies between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra.

questions.question: What do lines of latitude measure?
options: Distance north or south of the Equator
questions.explanation: Latitude is an angular position north or south of the Equator.

questions.question: What do lines of longitude measure?
options: Position east or west of the Prime Meridian
questions.explanation: Longitude describes east-west position.

questions.question: Which direction does a compass needle generally indicate?
questions.explanation: A compass needle aligns approximately with Earth's magnetic field.

questions.question: Which map feature explains symbols used on a map?
questions.explanation: The legend gives the meanings of map symbols.

questions.question: Which map feature helps estimate real-world distances?
questions.explanation: A map scale links map distances to ground distances.

questions.question: What type of climate is common in much of Malaysia?
questions.explanation: Malaysia lies near the Equator and generally has a tropical climate.

questions.question: Which ocean borders the western coast of the Americas?
questions.explanation: The Pacific lies west of North and South America.

questions.question: Which continent contains the Sahara Desert?
questions.explanation: The Sahara spans much of North Africa.

questions.question: What is an archipelago?
questions.explanation: An archipelago consists of multiple islands.

questions.question: Why do coastal regions often experience sea breezes during the day?
options: Land heats faster than the sea
questions.explanation: Differences in heating create pressure and airflow patterns.

questions.question: What causes day and night on Earth?
options: The Moon covering the Sun daily
questions.explanation: Earth rotates on its axis, turning places toward and away from the Sun.

questions.question: Which geographic feature is formed where a river deposits sediment near its mouth?
questions.explanation: River sediment can build a delta near the river mouth.

questions.question: Which renewable resource is strongly linked to windy coastal sites?
questions.explanation: Coastal winds can drive wind turbines where suitable.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of contour lines on a map?
questions.explanation: Contour lines join points of equal elevation.

questions.question: Why are mangroves valuable along tropical coasts?
options: They help protect shorelines and support habitats
questions.explanation: Mangroves can reduce erosion and provide wildlife habitat.
